title: A bass guitar against a synth bass

params.note: The bassline is original, not the 'Flash Light' part. The bass guitar is Karplus-Strong synthesis (a burst of noise circulating in a delay one period long); the synth is three detuned sawtooths into two low-passes with a filter envelope, gliding on the walk-down. Neither models a specific instrument's circuit. The 909 drums are a stand-in drummer.

caption: Same notes, same accents, same drums, so only the instrument changes. A sounds like a plucked string, which starts to fade the moment it is struck. B is a synthesizer: three buzzing oscillators and a filter that opens on every note. It holds its level for as long as the note is held, and it glides between the last notes, which no fretted string can do without a slide. In funk, where the bass carried the groove, that is a different instrument doing the same job. On 'Flash Light', Bernie Worrell played the bass part on linked Minimoogs, and Bootsy Collins, the band's bass player, played drums instead.
